company_context: Target Corporation is a large U.S. general-merchandise retailer. In spring 2022 it carried excess inventory after demand shifted away from discretionary categories (apparel, home, hardlines) it had over-ordered during the pandemic supply-chain scramble. In June 2022 Target publicly announced an aggressive plan to clear excess inventory through markdowns, cancellations, and added holding capacity, accepting near-term margin compression.
business_type: Large brick-and-mortar and omnichannel general-merchandise retail
time_period: Fiscal 2022 (year ended January 28, 2023), with first-quarter and second-quarter detail
macro_context: 2022 post-pandemic demand rotation from goods to services, elevated freight and inventory carrying costs, and high consumer-facing inflation that pressured discretionary spend.
outcome_category: 10 - margin/operational shock at an otherwise stable large firm (inventory glut and markdown-driven margin compression)
evidence_summary: Target entered fiscal 2022 with excess inventory: inventory was about $15.1 billion at the end of the first quarter (April 30, 2022), roughly 43 percent higher than a year earlier. The company responded with aggressive markdowns and cancellations, compressing margins: full-year gross margin rate fell to 23.6 percent in 2022 from 28.3 percent in 2021, with the decline reflecting higher clearance and promotional markdown rates including inventory impairments. Second-quarter operating margin rate fell to 1.2 percent from 9.8 percent a year earlier, driven by the gross-margin decline. By fiscal year-end inventory had been worked down to $13.5 billion (January 28, 2023) from $13.9 billion (January 29, 2022). This is a clean documented inventory-forecasting mismatch with quantified margin consequences and a corrective markdown program.

source_backed_metrics.q1_ending_inventory_apr_30_2022: approximately $15.1 billion (about 43 percent higher year over year)

owner_decision_context: Management chose to absorb sharp near-term margin damage to clear excess inventory quickly rather than carry it forward, announcing the markdown plan publicly in June 2022.
action_taken: Aggressive markdowns, order cancellations, and removal of excess inventory across discretionary categories during fiscal 2022, with added holding/distribution capacity.
outcome_evidence: Inventory was reduced from about $15.1 billion (Q1) to $13.5 billion at year-end, below the prior year's $13.9 billion; gross margin fell to 23.6 percent and quarterly operating margin briefly fell to 1.2 percent before recovering as the glut cleared.
source_limitations: Both the Target corporate 10-K MD&A page and SEC EDGAR returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch; full-year and quarterly figures were confirmed verbatim in Target corporate-domain and named-journalism (CNBC) search snippets rather than read in full text. The $15.1 billion and 43 percent Q1 figures come from Target's Q1 disclosure/earnings reporting rather than the 10-K full-year statements.

why_useful_for_opsiq: A textbook inventory_forecasting_mismatch at a healthy large retailer, with quantified margin compression and a deliberate corrective markdown program. Useful for testing whether OpsIQ correctly attributes the margin shock to inventory forecasting rather than to a structural demand or pricing-power failure, and for modeling adaptive re-evaluation triggered by a KPI deterioration that later normalizes.
